Missing word 'field' in the physics sense: the only root 'field' is 'piece of open farmland', so I used a loan ~field in the terms ~Higgs ~field and ~gluon ~field.

Missing words boson, photon, proton, gluon, elementary: all written as loans. 'elementary particle' is root particle KIND ~elementary; unclear whether a native build (e.g. particle KIND simple / base) was preferred.

No word for 'misleading': used deceive (노롬) with AGENT 'THAT statement' under REBUT. REBUT ('denies the target') is stronger than 'misleading', which does not say the statement is flatly false; no relation or root expresses 'true-ish but gives a wrong impression'.
No word for 'massless' and no clear rule for 'stays X': rendered as STILL NOT have AGENT photon THEME mass. mass.opp or lack (which means 'be without something needed') did not fit.

'unlike every other known elementary particle': rendered as ANDC CONTRAST 'NONE OTHER particle ... has spin 0'. Section 3 says NOT outranks amount words, so 'NOT have AGENT ALL OTHER ...' would have meant 'not all'; I had to switch to NONE. 'unlike' itself has no direct word.

'spin 0': unclear whether a quantum-number value should be written 'spin 0' (number straight after a root, section 11) or 'spin OF 0' / EQUAL THEME spin THAN 0 (measured-value pattern). I used 'have ... THEME spin 0'.

'at the LHC': unclear whether to attach it to the collaborations or to the announcing. There is no location linker inside a phrase, so I used OF NAME ~LHC on the team phrase ('teams ATLAS and CMS of the LHC'); 'at' is thereby weakened to 'of'.
Unclear whether KIND followed by a bracketed AND of two names, then OF, parses as intended: team KIND ( NAME A AND NAME B ) OF NAME LHC.

'about 99% of the mass of a proton': unsure between '99 percent' (root 르님 with a count) and 99 «%» (unit in notation). Used AROUND 99 percent NAMED handle OF ( mass OF proton ); unsure whether NAMED may sit between the head and a following OF when an AROUND + number precedes.

'comes from': no fitting verb (come = 'move toward here'), so I used the relational root source as predicate: source REL (99 percent ...) THEME (energy ...). Then 'not from the Higgs field' = BUT NOT source REL that-portion THEME Higgs-field.

Loan spelling, ç in François: the sheet says an accent follows its letter, but does not say whether a consonant with an accent still shares a block with the following vowel. I wrote c as its own block (너), then cedilla (뵤), then o and i as separate empty-initial blocks.

Loan spelling, W+ / W- / Z0: W is a vowel-class letter, so capital W is 여 + 으; unsure that a 'word' consisting of capital mark + one letter block + sign block satisfies the two-block minimum for loans without the filler 요.
Abbreviations ATLAS, CMS, LHC were marked with NAME, but QCD (a theory abbreviation) and the particle terms were not; the sheet does not say when an abbreviation counts as a proper name.
'Higgs boson' and 'Higgs field': unclear whether a term containing a personal name needs NAME; I wrote plain capitalised loans side by side, and NAME only for the person Peter Higgs.
'the 2013 Nobel Prize': written prize KIND NAME ~Nobel OF year 2013; unclear whether a year attaches with OF or as a WHEN role.

'had died' (pluperfect): no dedicated past-before-past form; used PAST ALREADY die ... WHEN year 2011. The semicolon link between the prize clause and the death clause is only ANDC; the implied 'which is why Brout did not share it' is not expressed (nor is it explicit in the English).
'their masses' rendered as mass OF SELF (SELF = AGENT of its own clause); unsure SELF is allowed inside an OF modifier.
Opener choice: used RECALLED for the factual sentences and TOLD for 'it is often said'; the task gives no source stance, so CLAIM would be equally defensible.

(All of the following is stated from memory.)

Ken Thompson and Dennis Ritchie wrote Unix at Bell Labs in 1969, on a PDP-7 computer with only 8 kB of memory. Licences to the Unix source code were given to several universities for a small price, because AT&T was forbidden at the time from selling software, and at UC Berkeley Bill Joy turned that code into BSD.

The file /etc/passwd and the command grep -r still work today in almost the same way as they did back then.

6B, 4A, 4B, 9A rely on the left-to-right order rule of section 3 (each particle covers everything on its right) rather than on explicit blocks; the sheet's later remark that a NOT/modal without a block 'covers only its own predicate' sits in some tension with that, but both rules give the intended reading here.

1A, 10A: rely on the rule that a bare NOT covers only its own predicate, so the CAUSE / FOR phrase stays outside the negation (as in the sheet's own example 2). The sheet also says a particle 'applies to everything on its right', so a reader could still pull the reason under NOT; I saw no bracket form that attaches a role phrase outside a NOT block.

11B: the sheet has no clause-level exclusive 'or' (XOR joins phrases only) and no way I could see to add 'and I do not know which' in the same sentence without mixing ORC and ANDC at one level. I wrote the wide-scope disjunction of two MUST clauses under CLAIM; the speaker's ignorance is implied, not stated, and ORC is inclusive.
6A: 'free to skip' is rendered with CAN over a NOT block (possible for us not to test); MAY over the same block would give the permission sense instead. The gloss mixes both.
9A: TIMES is not listed among the words that may take a block, so 'twice [not ring]' is forced only by left-to-right order (2 TIMES before NOT); 9B uses a NOT block around EXACT 2 TIMES.

2A, 4A/4B, 6B: where a modal and NOT are stacked, the sheet's two statements ('applies to everything on its right' vs 'without a block covers only its own predicate') pull slightly apart; I used explicit nested blocks in 2A, 6B, 7B and the sheet's own bare MUST NOT / NOT MUST order in 2B, 4A, 4B.

Vocabulary gaps filled by rule: valve and engineer are loans (뚜처띠, 이터보티이거); alarm = warn.tool; log = record.made; pump = pump.tool; 'ring' = emit sound; 'start the pump' = active + AGENT; 'attend' = come TO meet(ing); 'test passes' = fail.opp; 'deliberately' = intend with a block. 'He'/'she' are bound as man/woman with handles.
8B: I used the root hope with a THEME block rather than the HOPE attitude particle, because the sheet does not clearly allow an attitude particle after ANDC in mid-sentence.

General: the sheet has no explicit scope marker for header strength/attitude particles (LIKELY, HOPE) or for NOT/modals across ANDC-joined clauses, and it does not say whether a pre-predicate NOT reaches role phrases such as CAUSE/FOR. I avoided those by using predicates with { } blocks (probable, hope, intend, reason REL, true.opp, forbid) and by repeating the particle per clause.
1A/1B: NOT + CAUSE role phrase looked ambiguous, so I used 'reason REL { ... } THEME rain' as a second clause instead of the CAUSE role. 'leave' is arrive.opp from the derived list.

2A: 'forbid THEME { open ANDC activate }' plus an explicit second clause allowing 'only 1 act of those 2 acts'; the phrase 'ONLY 1 do OF THAT 2 do' is my own build and a bit clumsy. 'valve' is a loan (no root); 'start the pump' is active+AGENT on pump.tool.

3B/8B: relies on a clause joined with ANDC outside the closed { } block being at main level; I put the plainly asserted clause first to make that unmistakable. 8: 'passes' rendered as fail.opp (succeed).

6A: CAN covers both 'able' and 'possible in fact'; 'CAN NOT test' = it is possible/able for us not to test. If the reading should be permission, MAY (캬) in place of CAN (커) would be the alternative.

7: 'engineer' is a loan. 7B relies on NOT before believe not being neg-raised into the block; the sheet's right-scope rule supports that but the sheet has no way to add 'may have no opinion' short of another clause.

9: 'alarm' built as warn.tool, 'ring' as 'emit THEME sound' (no roots). 9B uses NOT EXACT 2 TIMES; ordering of NOT and TIMES by the 'applies to everything on its right' rule is what separates A and B.

11A: MUST over a bracketed OR phrase alone might still be read as B, so I added 'and the guard MAY choose the thing the guard checks'. 11B: the sheet has no wide-scope OR over a modal except clause-level ORC; I wrapped the ORC pair in 'true THEME { ... }' to avoid mixing ORC and BUT at one level, and stated the speaker's ignorance with an embedded question. ORC is inclusive, so 'one specific duty' is not strictly forced (XOR joins only phrases).

I therefore avoided role phrases for reason/purpose/manner (items 1, 5, 10) and expressed them as a separate predicate (cause, intend) with { } blocks, and put the negated clause last wherever two clauses are joined.

4: no root for 'attend'; written as 'come TO meet(ing)'.
